reforms.description: The Canadian government announced measures in the April 1978 budget and reinforced them in the November 1978 budget to stimulate research and development expenditure, providing increased investment and R&D incentives to support corporate investment in R&D. These measures were introduced in response to recommendations from the First Ministers' Conference task forces.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax incentives and direct investment support increase private sector R&D capacity and productivity, supporting innovation and long-term economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states measures were 'announced' in April 1978 budget and November 1978 budget; no evidence of implementation provided.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant fiscal measures announced across two budgets in 1978 to stimulate R&D, but not a structural system-wide reform.
reforms.source_quote: The Government agreed in principle with the vast majority of these proposals, and in the November 1978 Budget responded to several of the recommendations, including the provision of increased investment as well as research and development incentives.

reforms.description: The Enterprise Development Programme provides innovation assistance to firms undertaking research and development projects through grants covering up to one-half of product development costs (or three-quarters for small firms).
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Direct grants for product development reduce financial barriers to R&D investment, particularly for small firms, supporting innovation and commercialisation.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states the programme 'provides' assistance, indicating it is in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant innovation support programme with differentiated support for small firms, but not a system-wide structural reform.
reforms.source_quote: On the one hand, it provides innovation assistance in the form of grants up to one-half (or three-quarters for small firms) of product development costs.
